paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty terms across six medical specialties, comparing a base model (Mistralv0.2-Base) against versions fine-tuned on each of the six specialties. The horizontal axis is labeled "Per-specialty terms" and contains six categorical groups: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis is labeled "Negative log probability" and uses a linear scale ranging from approximately -27 to -22, with tick marks at integer intervals. Within each group, seven bars are displayed: a light blue bar representing Mistralv0.2-Base, followed by six bars representing models fine-tuned on Cardio (light yellow), Gastro (light peach/tan), Infect (medium orange), Neuro (darker orange), Obstetrics (dark brown-orange), and Pediatrics (dark brown). Across all six specialty groups, the light blue Mistralv0.2-Base bar consistently reaches approximately -22, making it the tallest (least negative) bar in every group. The fine-tuned model bars vary in height across groups; for example, in the Cardio group, the fine-tuned bars range from approximately -22.5 down to about -26.2, with the Cardio fine-tuned model (light yellow) reaching roughly -22.5 and the Gastro fine-tuned model reaching approximately -26.2. In the Infect group, the bars are generally closer to -22, with most fine-tuned models reaching around -22.5 to -24.5. In the Neuro group, values range from approximately -22.5 to -25. The Obstetrics and Pediatrics groups show similar patterns with fine-tuned bars spanning roughly -23 to -25. The bars within each group are not sorted by value but rather follow a consistent ordering based on the legend sequence. No bars appear to be visually emphasized through bolding or outlining beyond the color-coding described in the legend.
